title: Study Baseline
description: The measurement every arm in the study is compared against. Set once, before any arm is judged, because a delta without a baseline is a number with nothing on the other side of the minus sign.

execution_id.description: The execution that produced this measurement, so a later reader can locate it.

metric.description: Must name the protocol's primary metric. A baseline in some other unit is not a baseline for this study.

provenance.description: Checked in code: a baseline must be `measured`. Comparing every arm against a modelled number means the whole study is measuring its own prediction.

profile.description: Path to the profile captured alongside the baseline. Required, not optional. Without it the first round has no per-op attribution, so it cannot rank arms by headroom and falls back to guessing which layer to attack -- which is the failure the whole design exists to avoid.

fingerprint.description: What this baseline is a baseline OF. Recorded so a later study can tell whether this one is reusable rather than re-measuring something that already exists -- an end-to-end run costs hours, so the answer matters.

config_digest.description: Digest of the serving or training configuration. Matching on a hash is only as good as the normalisation under it, so the scheme must be stated wherever it is produced.

cell.description: The measurement cell, as topology and workload shape. The same sha and config on different hardware is a different baseline.

adopted_from_run.description: Set when this baseline was reused rather than measured by this study. An adopted baseline must be visibly adopted: a silently reused number is how a study ends up comparing against something nobody can locate.
